clue.text: Title rumoured for composer

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so the word for title is heard rather than read

parts.note: a handle is slang for a title or name

explanation.surface: Gossip about an honorary title being given to a famous composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumoured' signals a soundalike: HANDLE, slang for a name or title, sounds like HANDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: Worry mustang's tempted to bite

indicators.note: biting takes a piece out of something, so the answer is taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A worry that a wild horse is tempted to bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is anxiety or dread, a deep sort of worry.

clue.text: Busy? Not working, with time for fun principally!

indicators.note: with one thing for another means a swap, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: defective means faulty, not working

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Busy? No, not working, more interested in having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSY is British slang for a detective. 'for' swaps the F in DEFECTIVE for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy is British slang for a police detective; the question mark flags the slang.

clue.text: Bridge close to Swiss golf course

parts.note: a link is a connection, a bridge between things

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bridge near a Swiss golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Links is a seaside golf course, the traditional type in Scotland.

clue.text: Shortened career over your foul

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the trimmed word is read backwards
shortened means cut off at the end, so the last letter of the career word is dropped

parts.note: a career is one's working life
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Someone's career was cut short because of foul behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a job but stands for one's whole working life; 'Shortened' drops its last letter and 'over' turns the rest round.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul and filthy are synonyms for disgustingly dirty.

clue.text: Crooked thief's protecting fool that's lifted sandwich spread

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so the anagram encloses the other piece
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, lifted means raised up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a sap is a fool

explanation.surface: A crooked thief shields a fool who stole the sandwich filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suggests stealing but, in a down clue, turns the fool word upwards; 'Crooked' rearranges THIEF'S around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish paste is a savoury spread used in sandwiches.

clue.text: Able to go topless in bar

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, which in a down clue is the first letter

parts.note: clever means able

explanation.surface: A bar that allows people to go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the C from CLEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar used to pry or lift things.

clue.text: Enable European to stop female making annual event

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters go inside the female

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
to allow is to enable

explanation.surface: Letting a European halt a woman's yearly celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is the festival on 31 October, held every year.

clue.text: Criticise dog name this writer's introducing

indicators.note: introducing means coming in front, so these letters lead the dog and name

parts.note: this writer is is I'M
a pug is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A writer brings in a dog and a name, then criticises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is the setter saying I am, shortened to IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to call into question or attack as false.

clue.text: Cartoonist maybe up for prize

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cartoonist is an example of a drawer, one who draws

explanation.surface: A cartoonist is in the running for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like in contention, but it reverses DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a prize given in return for something.

clue.text: Car manufacturer employs one that's oddly lacking ability

indicators.note: a firm that employs someone takes them inside, so the car maker's letters hold the numeral

parts.note: MG is the British car marque
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: lacking the odd letters means only the even-placed letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A car company takes on a worker who, strangely, has no skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employs' puts the numeral inside the car marque; 'oddly lacking' discards the odd-placed letters of THAT'S, keeping the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Might means power or capability, a synonym of ability.

clue.text: Remains very unwell visiting north-eastern US city

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so these letters go between the two compass letters

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone's remains, or a very sick person, are on a trip to an American city in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north-eastern' looks like part of the definition, but it gives NE, which surrounds ASH, V and ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of Tennessee, famous for country music.

clue.text: At university work facing students ultimately increases

parts.note: up means at university, as in going up to Oxford
to tick is to work or function, as in what makes someone tick

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A student at university working with fellow students.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at university' is a British usage: one goes up to a university and comes down at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Upticks are small rises, a term used in finance for price increases.

clue.text: Grapes mostly cultivated outside over large garden feature

indicators.note: outside means the anagram goes around the next letters
cultivated means worked or tilled, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Grapes grown over a large structure in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts GRAPES to GRAPE; 'cultivated' turns that into PERGA, and 'outside' puts it around O and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is an arched framework in a garden that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Retired South American, so it's written, managed plant

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: US means American
sic is Latin for thus, used to mean so it is written
ran means managed

explanation.surface: A retired South American ran things, as the records say, growing a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one person but gives S and US separately; 'Retired' reverses S US SIC RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcissus is a bulb plant, the genus that includes daffodils.

clue.text: Cool drink ordered here's free virtually, right?

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are rearranged
virtually means almost, so the last letter of free is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone orders a cold drink and asks if it is nearly free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' cuts FREE to FRE; with HERE'S, 'ordered' makes REFRESHE, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is a drink that refreshes, especially a cooling one.

clue.text: Son obsessed essentially with flipping hidden Roman coins

indicators.note: essentially points to the central letters of the word
flipping means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: secret means hidden

explanation.surface: An obsessive son with hidden Roman coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes ES from the middle of OBSESSED; 'flipping' turns SECRET to TERCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesterces were silver, later brass, coins of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Quietly direct what courtroom defendant must do

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quietly
to lead is to direct

explanation.surface: A quiet instruction about how a defendant should behave in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant must enter a plea, stating guilty or not guilty before trial.

clue.text: Vote Paul rigged to keep student in athletics event

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the anagram contains the letter
a rigged vote is fixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A rigged vote for Paul to keep a student in an athletics competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' turns VOTE PAUL into POVAULTE, which holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Pole vault is a track and field event jumping a bar with a pole.

clue.text: Slip when I run to escape large creature

indicators.note: escaping means leaving, so these letters are taken out of the animal

parts.note: a giraffe is a large animal
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A slip happens when someone runs to get away from a big beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I and R from GIRAFFE leaves GAFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, a slip in speech or behaviour.

clue.text: Bribe EU member, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means spoken out, so the country's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Greece is a member state of the European Union

explanation.surface: Bribing a European Union member, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: GREECE sounds like GREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease, as in greasing palms, is slang for a bribe.

clue.text: The littlest ones growing up in a nursery?

definitions.text: The littlest ones growing up in a nursery?

parts.words: The littlest ones growing up in a nursery?
parts.note: suggests infants in a children's nursery, but a plant nursery raises young plants

explanation.surface: Small children being raised in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is a garden nursery, not a children's one; its smallest growing things are young plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedlings are young plants grown from seed, the youngest stock in a plant nursery.

clue.text: Is my team regularly adopting somewhat vacuous approach?

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the regular letters hold the other pair
regularly means every other letter is taken
vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Is my team taking a fairly empty-headed approach?
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat vacuous' reads as one phrase, but 'vacuous' empties the word SOMEWHAT to its ends; 'adopting' puts those inside the regular letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or approach to doing something.

clue.text: Raise cheer to welcome English victor

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or make happy
V is victor in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheer is raised to greet an English winner.
explanation.walkthrough: V for victor comes from the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift or raise something higher.

clue.text: Bolt vegetables once peeled

indicators.note: peeling removes the outer skin, so the first and last letters are taken off

parts.note: marrows are large vegetables

explanation.surface: Vegetables that have been peeled are quickly gobbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like eating fast but is a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt is a short arrow shot from a crossbow.

clue.text: Trainee nuns, their condition of acceptance by convent?

definitions.meaning: those training to take religious vows

definitions.text: their condition of acceptance by convent?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., the requirement a convent might impose

explanation.surface: Novice nuns must be free of vices to be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as NO VICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are probationary members of a religious order before final vows.

clue.text: Material many Londoners will acquire

indicators.note: acquiring means holding, so the answer is held in these words

explanation.surface: A fabric that plenty of Londoners will buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre used to make fabric.

clue.text: Stop fugitive finally packing trunk

indicators.note: a case packing something holds it inside

parts.note: a trunk is a large case for luggage

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fugitive stops to pack a trunk at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or come to an end.

clue.text: Pub Heather left after sister's initial round

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the letter from sister's
initial means the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house
erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: Heather left the pub after her sister's first name was called.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means shaped like a ball, which is round.

clue.text: Posh philosopher finds employment

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U
a sage is a wise person or philosopher

explanation.surface: An upper-class thinker gets a job.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh comes from the British upper-class versus non-U distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means use or employment of something, as in the usage of a word.

clue.text: Scraps tools Bill offloaded

indicators.note: offloaded means got rid of, so these letters are dropped from the tools

parts.note: bradawls are small boring tools
an ad is a bill or poster advertisement

explanation.surface: Bill gets rid of scraps and tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' looks like leftovers but means fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps and brawls are both rough fights.

clue.text: Spice seen in stone cask from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Spice found inside a stone barrel imported from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' suggests the spice's origin; it reverses GEMTUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the seed of a tropical tree, ground as a spice.
